dimension_justifications.soundness: The finite-domain selector, boundary cardinalities, half-step median discussion, and displayed NFE arithmetic are internally coherent. However, the central lock-time coordinate and missing/terminal-case semantics are unresolved, all empirical values are source-reported and locally unverifiable, and the probe argmaxes lack complete candidate vectors. These gaps prevent reliable validation of the central descriptive result.
dimension_justifications.presentation: The PDF is readable, anonymous, within the nine-page main-text limit, and contains useful figures, consolidated tables, explicit limitations, and terminology crosswalks. Nevertheless, the paper's identity is obscured by switching among a scientific report, an audit of a separate 'source manuscript,' and a revision report. Repeated SR/CV caveats and duplicated limitations dominate the narrative, while several secondary analyses interrupt the central argument.
dimension_justifications.contribution: The distinction between a-priori boundary-set reachability and event-dependent magnitude is useful, but the empirical contribution is a narrow one-model, one-task, active-recorder case study under a composite intervention. The paper establishes no mechanism, and its incomplete closest-work audit leaves distinctness from prior measurement-confound work uncertain.

paper_summary: The paper studies identity-lock-time profiles from an active-block recorder in blockwise diffusion-language-model decoding. At fixed canvas, total NFE, decoding rule, and questions, it changes block length together with the required per-block allocation and applies a min-boundary-minus-max-interior selector over candidate periods. It reports P*=L for L16/L64 main arms, a reused L32 development control, and sequential L24/L48 probes, with a same-profile rank-sum ordering giving the same reported choices. The paper carefully limits this to recorder-observable schedule alignment, not a model or sampler mechanism, and recommends separating algebraic reachability from empirical magnitude.
strongest_verified_contribution: The clearest verifiable contribution is the conceptual and notational separation between a-priori boundary-set composition and conclusions that require measured magnitudes. From the printed definitions, the candidate-set cardinalities and all displayed per-block schedule sums are internally consistent, and the complete canvas-256 candidate rows do yield their printed argmaxes. This does not independently verify the empirical cell values themselves.
strengths: The manuscript is unusually explicit about evidence stratification: reused development control, main arms, sequential probes, and separate content bed are not presented as equivalent replications.
Equations (1) and (2), the finite domains, tie rule, admissibility condition, and the distinction between bootstrap stability and false-positive control are stated clearly.
The discussion of midpoint medians is correct: with n=300, half-integral medians, differences, and separations are possible, while integer observations do not force a bootstrap point mass.

The schedule arithmetic in Table 1 is correct: L16 gives 8x4+8x2=48, L64 gives 16+16+8+8=48, L32/NFE48 gives 4x8+4x4=48, and the canvas-96 probe schedules also sum to 48. The printed boundary/interior cardinalities also match their finite domains.
Figure 1 communicates the recorder-window intuition effectively and is explicitly labeled qualitative; Figure 2 and the main result tables are legible and captions disclose their evidentiary limits.
The submission is anonymous, uses letter-sized ICLR-style formatting, ends the main text on page 9 before references, and includes an AI-assisted-preparation disclosure on PDF page 16.
questions: What exactly does the step label s in Ti,r denote: global function-evaluation index, block-local iteration, or position-observation ordinal? How are empty, censored, terminal, and unresolved cases encoded, and can Ar vary with r?
Is the intended paper an empirical study, an artifact audit of an inherited study, or a revision/provenance report? What entity does 'source manuscript' refer to relative to the submitted paper?
Can the authors provide all six sep(P) and rank-sum candidate scores for each L24/L48 probe, including the exact tie and normalization rules?
What is the ordered per-block schedule for the L32/NFE32 content bed? Is it eight blocks with four evaluations each?
Which additional primary papers were examined when determining that active-recorder identity-lock periodicity and this intervention are distinct from prior measurement-confound diagnostics?

issues.location: PDF pp. 3-4, Section 2, 'Identity-lock time and finite observation domain,' Eq. (1), especially lines 146-159; PDF p. 8, Limitations, 'Event semantics'; PDF p. 16, Appendix B, 'Reported determinism claim'
issues.observed_evidence: The manuscript explicitly states that the package does not establish whether s is global, block-local, or a position-observation ordinal and lacks rules for empty observations, missing final values, censoring, terminal cases, and analyzed-decode membership. The reviewer-safe method record A31-M1 confirms these semantics and implementation are unavailable.
issues.why_it_matters: The coordinate convention determines whether lock times are comparable across positions and whether block transitions can create the reported adjacent-difference periodicity. Position-dependent inclusion can also make d(r) compare medians over different populations. Thus the central measurement is mathematically named but not operationally reproducible or fully interpretable.
issues.required_fix: Specify the event schema, clock domain, observation ordering, final-value rule, censoring/terminal handling, and whether the analyzed set is position-dependent. Supply a small raw trace illustrating every case and state the exact implementation of Eq. (1).
issues.verification_test: Using the supplied trace and implementation, independently reconstruct every ell_i,r, then m(r), d(r), and sep(P). Recompute the headline tables under the documented convention and at least one plausible alternative clock convention; verify that the reported P*=L conclusions are unchanged or narrow the claim accordingly.
issues.evidence_needed: Event-schema specification, representative raw events, inclusion/exclusion manifest, lock-time implementation, and regenerated result hashes.

issues.location: PDF p. 2, Section 2, 'Numerical provenance'; PDF pp. 5-7, Tables 2-6 and Figure 2; PDF pp. 12 and 16, Tables 9 and 14; reviewer-safe repository inventory and experiment registry
issues.observed_evidence: Every empirical number is marked SR/CV. The package lacks event streams, analysis programs, result arrays, pairing manifests, replicate indicators, registration records, and Figure 2's data/generator. The manuscript states that no analysis was rerun.
issues.why_it_matters: The paper's central empirical association, uncertainty summaries, sensitivity checks, and registration chronology cannot be independently checked. This is a cannot_verify limitation rather than evidence that the printed values are false, but it caps confidence and makes the paper non-reproducible in its current form.
issues.required_fix: Release a reviewer-safe evidence bundle containing de-identified inputs or sufficient event extracts, exact configurations, executable analysis code, machine-readable result vectors, seeds, bootstrap/permutation outputs, and figure-generation code.
issues.verification_test: Run the documented pipeline from a clean environment and require exact reproduction, within declared stochastic tolerances, of Tables 2-7 and 10-14 plus Figure 2. Check that the paired-bootstrap indicators reproduce both marginal and joint summaries.
issues.evidence_needed: Executable artifact, machine-readable outputs, environment lock, seeds, logs, and result/figure hashes.

issues.location: Title and Abstract on PDF p. 1; Introduction on pp. 1-2; repeated 'source manuscript,' 'accessible package,' and 'this revision' framing throughout Sections 2-6; Appendix B on p. 16
issues.observed_evidence: The submission alternates between presenting a scientific study and auditing an inaccessible inherited 'source manuscript.' The abstract leads with package limitations, while the same qualifications—SR/CV status, incomplete probe vectors, non-independence of rank-sum, composite intervention, and no mechanism claim—are repeated across the abstract, introduction, method, results, limitations, conclusion, captions, and appendix.
issues.why_it_matters: Readers cannot quickly determine the paper's primary identity, ownership of the experiment, or headline contribution. Extensive repetition consumes the page budget and obscures the actual method, result, and practical recommendation.
issues.required_fix: Choose and state one paper identity. If this is an artifact audit, retitle and structure it explicitly as such; if it is the empirical study, use direct authorial voice and centralize provenance limitations in one concise auditability statement. Rewrite the abstract around problem, intervention, principal result, and scope; remove repeated caveats after their first operative occurrence.
issues.verification_test: Confirm that title, final abstract sentence, introduction contribution list, Results headings, and conclusion express the same one-sentence identity. Search for the repeated provenance phrases and retain each limitation only where it changes interpretation. Have an independent reader summarize the intervention, result, and non-claim without consulting the appendix.
issues.evidence_needed: A reorganized manuscript with a single narrative voice and deduplicated limitation statements.

issues.location: PDF p. 1, Abstract; p. 6, Table 3 probe rows; p. 7, Table 4; p. 8, Section 3.2 and 'Probe auditability' limitation; PDF p. 12, Table 9
issues.observed_evidence: The paper reports P*=24 and P*=48 and matching rank-sum choices for the probes, but prints no complete six-candidate sep or rank-sum vectors. Table 3 correctly uses dashes, and Table 4 supplies only sep(32) plus one mismatched L24 cell. L24 is marginal under pmargin and L48 has a single selected boundary locus.
issues.why_it_matters: The probe argmaxes are part of the headline contribution and are used to address nesting, yet they cannot be reconstructed from the submission. The two probes therefore remain assertions rather than auditable candidate comparisons.
issues.required_fix: Print or release the full ordered sep(P) and rank-sum vectors for P in {8,16,24,32,48,64}, including ties, boundary cardinalities, bootstrap mode counts, and the exact rank-sum definition.
issues.verification_test: Independently compute both argmaxes using the registered order and tie rule, verify top-minus-second margins, and confirm the reported modal-period fractions from replicate-level outputs.
issues.evidence_needed: Complete probe candidate vectors, rank-sum implementation, replicate-level selections, and de-identified probe profiles.

issues.location: PDF p. 9, Section 5, Related Work; PDF p. 15, Table 13; citation_lock.json
issues.observed_evidence: Related Work provides only three narrow checked comparisons, and both the manuscript and citation lock explicitly say that bibliography-wide metadata and sentence-level support auditing remain incomplete. No priority claim is made, which is responsible, but the closest-work boundary is consequently not established.
issues.why_it_matters: The empirical scope is already narrow, so the case for contribution depends heavily on whether the measurement object, schedule perturbation, and reachability/magnitude reporting rule differ materially from prior diagnostics. The current included citation material cannot verify that boundary.
issues.required_fix: Complete a primary-source literature audit covering diffusion-decoding diagnostics, commitment/lock-time measurements, schedule-induced periodicity, active-window instrumentation artifacts, and finite-grid period selection. Expand the closest-work matrix to compare measurement object, intervention, estimand, and conclusion.
issues.verification_test: For every novelty-positioning sentence, provide verified metadata and a source-supported local-use record. Check that the abstract and introduction make no broader novelty claim than the completed matrix supports.
issues.evidence_needed: Completed citation lock, sentence-level support audit, and expanded closest-work comparison.

issues.location: PDF p. 3, Table 1, Content-bed column; PDF pp. 13-15, Sections A.7-A.8
issues.observed_evidence: Table 1 says it consolidates every bed and schedule, but the L32/NFE32 content-bed cell shows only '32' in the combined 'L; ordered per-block steps' row. Unlike every NFE48 arm, it does not display the ordered step vector or arithmetic sum.
issues.why_it_matters: The reader cannot tell from the configuration table how eight L32 blocks consume 32 evaluations, weakening cross-section consistency for the supporting content analysis.
issues.required_fix: Separate block length from ordered steps in Table 1 and print the content-bed schedule and sum explicitly, for example eight four-step blocks if that is the actual configuration.
issues.verification_test: Check that every canvas/NFE pair has a step vector whose length equals its number of blocks and whose sum equals total NFE, and cross-check it against the launcher configuration.

issues.location: PDF p. 4, Section 2, line 168; PDF p. 7, Table 6 caption; PDF pp. 12 and 17, Sections A.4 and C/Table 15
issues.observed_evidence: 'Strictly L-supported' is used in the main method before its operative condition is fully explained. Its later definition is split across a table caption, Appendix A.4, and the terminology table, whose location pointer says Section 3.1.
issues.why_it_matters: This condition is essential to the claimed divisor/multiple behavior, so delayed and distributed definition makes the logical boundary harder to follow.
issues.required_fix: Define 'strictly L-supported' formally at first use next to Eq. (2), and make all glossary and cross-reference pointers target that single definition.
issues.verification_test: Read Sections 1-3 without appendices and confirm that every specialized term needed to understand the headline selector is defined before use and referenced consistently.
issues.evidence_needed: A localized terminology and cross-reference revision.

ethics_concerns: No specific human-subject, safety, privacy, or societal-risk concern is apparent from the frozen submission. The private checkpoint and missing artifacts are reproducibility concerns rather than an identified ethics violation.
llm_usage_disclosure: This review was produced by a fresh, isolated AI reviewer for internal pre-submission quality control, with read-only access to the frozen snapshot. The paper itself discloses AI assistance for language editing, LaTeX refactoring, internal review, and an inherited image-generated qualitative Figure 1; no undisclosed empirical AI verification was inferred.
evidence_that_would_raise_score: A reviewer-safe artifact that cleanly reproduces the identity-lock profiles, complete candidate vectors, bootstrap summaries, sensitivity analyses, and Figure 2.
A precise event-time and missing/terminal-case contract, with robustness showing P*=L under the declared coordinate and reasonable alternative encodings.
Complete L24/L48 separation and rank-sum vectors that independently reproduce both reported probe choices and margins.
A completed primary-source literature audit establishing a clear distinction from prior schedule, recorder, and commitment-time diagnostics.
A reorganized manuscript with a single paper identity, substantially less repeated provenance language, and a sharper mapping from each contribution to one result.

For a score above 6, a fresh control or cross-recorder/factorial experiment that separates recorder-window effects from partition/allocation effects and broadens the evidence beyond one model-task setting.
evidence_that_would_lower_score: Reanalysis showing that global versus local time labels or position-dependent missingness changes the selected periods.
Machine-readable probe vectors in which L24 or L48 is not the registered argmax, or the rank-sum ordering depends on an undisclosed tie/normalization choice.
Replicate-level outputs that fail to reproduce the reported marginal or joint bootstrap summaries.
Evidence that the reused development control influenced estimator selection more extensively than the disclosed chronology indicates.
Verified prior work that already establishes the same active-recorder confound, intervention, and reporting principle, leaving only a replication-level contribution.
review_limitations: Per instruction, no internet, parent directory, repository history, prior review, author note, or revision record was inspected; novelty assessment is limited to the included citation lock and PDF.

The package intentionally omits raw events, executable analyses, complete probe vectors, registration records, and the private checkpoint, so empirical correctness was assessed only for internal consistency and disclosed audit boundaries.
The PDF was read in full and all 17 pages were visually inspected, but source-level LaTeX compliance could not be checked because only source hashes, not source files, were included.
